title: Asking the pope (1887)
hookLine: everyone in line is told to stay silent; a girl from France has a request, and her sister whispers: speak
tomorrow: the pope said 'if God wills.' so did the door open?

cards: There's always a rule about who gets to talk. Wait to be called on. Players don't argue with the ref.
No questions at the end. A long line of pilgrims moves past an old man in white, and everyone has been told the same thing: kneel, receive his blessing, and say nothing.
A girl in the line has a request she has carried all the way from France. Her sister leans in and whispers one word: speak.

teach.b: First, the closed doors. Thérèse wanted to enter Carmel young. The priest in charge of the convent said wait, and the bishop hadn't said yes.
So she went to Rome on pilgrimage with her father and Céline. Second, the request.
Kneeling before Pope Leo the Thirteenth, despite the order to keep silent, she asked: Most Holy Father, in honor of your jubilee, let me enter Carmel at fifteen.
Third, the answer. The vicar general nearby said the superiors were already looking into it. The pope told her, kindly, to do what the superiors said.
She pressed. He looked at her and said she would enter if God willed it. Then the guards led her away, in tears.
Fourth, the ball. She had offered herself to the child Jesus as his little ball, a toy he could play with, leave in a corner, or prick to see inside.
In Rome, she says, he pricked his little ball, let it fall, and went to sleep.
She asked boldly, and left the answer with God.

how: Catholics go on pilgrimage to Rome and to shrines, and at a papal audience pilgrims may receive the pope's blessing; asking God boldly in prayer is encouraged by Jesus's 'ask, and it shall be given you.'

o: her vow of silence as a young Carmelite
a letter she wrote to the bishop of her town
her bold request to the pope, against the rules

games.q: the audience in Rome — tap the pairs.
p: you'll enter if God wills it
the superiors are looking into it
pricked in Rome, then let fall

s: the pope said yes and let her enter Carmel right away
he said she would enter if God willed it, and the guards led her away in tears.
the pilgrims had been told not to speak to the pope
she spoke anyway, after Céline whispered: speak.
Thérèse says she felt no disappointment in Rome
she says Jesus pricked his little ball and let it fall.

games.q: you asked your coach boldly for a starting spot and got 'we'll see.' you're crushed. what's Thérèse's little-ball image for?
o: holding a no-for-now honestly, without pretending, and trusting anyway.
proof that bold asking never works, so it's better not to ask.
a sign to keep pushing every day until the answer is yes.
games.why: she cried, didn't pretend it didn't hurt, and called herself a ball pricked and let fall: the answer left with God.

practice: Walk slowly for a minute, around a room or down a hall, carrying one good thing you've been afraid to ask for, the way she carried hers down that line. When you stop, say it once, plainly, out loud.
If you pray, you can bring it with Jesus's words in Matthew: Ask, and it shall be given you.

wordCard.voice: Asking the pope. Thérèse's bold request to Leo the Thirteenth, against the rule to keep silent.

carryVoice: The line to keep: she asked the pope, boldly, with an open hand for the answer. Bye for now.
